citation.author: Thompson, D.W.
citation.title: On Growth and Form
citation.chapter: XVII — On the Theory of Transformations

state_variables.u: Cartesian x in a leaf outline coordinate frame (petiole at origin, tip along +y)
state_variables.y0: Radial coordinate pole offset (arrest/base point on petiole axis)
state_variables.rho: sqrt(u^2 + (v - y0)^2) — radial distance from arrest point
state_variables.phi: atan2(u, v - y0) — polar angle about arrest point
state_variables.k: Tangential angle scaling (cordate bilobing when k > 1)

governing_equations.latex: x' = a_1 \rho \sin(k\phi) + a_2 \rho \cos\phi \sin(k\phi) + t_x;\; y' = b_1 \rho \cos(k\phi) + b_2 \rho \cos\phi \cos(k\phi) + t_y

boundary_conditions: Petiole insertion fixed at the radial pole (u=0, v=y0 maps to transformed stem point)
Closed outline sampled CCW with tip at maximum v
empirical_claims: Lanceolate, ovate and cordate leaves are mutual transforms under one radial coordinate system
Begonia leaf exemplifies the same radial transformation family
